question.problem:
The lengths of babies at birth in a given population are normally distributed with a mean of $\mu \,\text{cm}$ and a standard deviation of $6\,\text{cm}.$ Additionally, the length of $60%$ of the newborns falls between $0.9\mu \,\text{cm}$ and $1.1\mu \,\text{cm}.$ Find the mean $\mu $ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the length of a randomly selected newborn. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{6}^{2}),$ and we want to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu )=0.6.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.6 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.6 \\ P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.3 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.5+0.3 \\ P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.8\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.8 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.1\mu }{6}) & =0.8 \\ Φ(\frac{0.1\mu }{6}) & =0.8 \\ \frac{0.1\mu }{6} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.8)≈0.8416.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.1\mu }{6} & =0.8416 \\ 0.1\mu  & =5.0496 \\ \mu  & =\frac{5.0496}{0.1} \\  & ≈50.50\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$
